sentences.chinese: 慕容廆
sentences.literal: Murong Hui.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui

sentences.chinese: 慕容廆，字弈洛瑰，昌黎棘城鮮卑人也。
sentences.literal: Murong Hui, style Yiluogui, was a Xianbei man from Jicheng in Changli commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hui, courtesy Yiluogui, was a Xianbei from Jicheng in Changli.

sentences.chinese: 其先有熊氏之苗裔，世居北夷，邑于紫蒙之野，號曰東胡。
sentences.literal: His ancestors were descendants of the Youxiong clan; for generations they dwelt among the northern Yi, with a settlement in the wilds of Zimeng, called the Eastern Hu.
sentences.idiomatic: They traced their line to the Youxiong and lived beyond the frontier in Zimeng, a people known as the Eastern Hu.

sentences.chinese: 其後與匈奴並盛，控弦之士二十餘萬，風俗官號與匈奴略同。
sentences.literal: Later they flourished alongside the Xiongnu; bow-gripping warriors exceeded two hundred thousand; customs and official titles were broadly similar to the Xiongnu.
sentences.idiomatic: They grew as strong as the Xiongnu, fielding more than two hundred thousand archers, with similar customs and titles.

sentences.chinese: 秦漢之際為匈奴所敗，分保鮮卑山，因以為號。
sentences.literal: At the Qin-Han transition they were defeated by the Xiongnu, split off to hold Mount Xianbei, and thereby took it as their name.
sentences.idiomatic: Beaten by the Xiongnu at the fall of Qin, they withdrew to Mount Xianbei and took that name.

sentences.chinese: 曾祖莫護跋，魏初率其諸部入居遼西，從宣帝伐公孫氏有功，拜率義王，始建國於棘城之北。
sentences.literal: His great-grandfather Mohuba, at the beginning of Wei, led his various tribes to enter and dwell in Liaoxi; following Emperor Xuan he campaigned against the Gongsun clan with merit, was appointed Prince of Shuaiyi, and first established a state north of Jicheng.
sentences.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Mohuba brought the tribes into Liaoxi under Wei, fought the Gongsuns for Emperor Xuan, received the title Prince of Shuaiyi, and founded their seat north of Jicheng.

sentences.chinese: 時燕代多冠步搖冠，莫護跋見而好之，乃斂發襲冠，諸部因呼之為步搖，其後音訛，遂為慕容焉。
sentences.literal: At that time Yan and Dai often wore swaying-step crowns; Mohuba saw them and liked them; thereupon he bound hair and donned the crown; the various tribes therefore called him Buyao; afterward the sound corrupted, and it became Murong.
sentences.idiomatic: Mohuba admired the Han-style swaying crown and wore it; tribes called him “Buyao,” which later slurred into “Murong.”

sentences.chinese: 或云慕二儀之德，繼三光之容，遂以慕容為氏。
sentences.literal: Some say they admired the virtue of the Two Patterns and continued the countenance of the Three Luminaries, and thereby took Murong as surname.
sentences.idiomatic: Another etymology links the name to reverence for Heaven and Earth and the sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.chinese: 祖木延，左賢王。
sentences.literal: His grandfather Muyan was Left Worthy King.
sentences.idiomatic: His grandfather Muyan held the Xiongnu-style title of Left Worthy King.

sentences.chinese: 父涉歸，以全柳城之功，進拜鮮卑單于，遷邑於遼東北，於是漸慕諸夏之風矣。
sentences.literal: His father Shegui, for merit in preserving Liucheng, was advanced and appointed Xianbei Shanyu, moved the settlement to the northeast of Liaodong, and thereby gradually admired the airs of the Hua domains.
sentences.idiomatic: His father Shegui earned promotion to Xianbei Shanyu for saving Liucheng, moved the capital toward eastern Liaodong, and began adopting Chinese ways.

sentences.chinese: 廆幼而魁岸，美姿貌，身長八尺，雄傑有大度。
sentences.literal: Hui in youth was towering, handsome in bearing, eight chi in height, heroic and large in capacity.
sentences.idiomatic: From boyhood he was tall and striking—eight feet of frame—with the bearing of a born leader.

sentences.chinese: 安北將軍張華雅有知人之鑒，廆童丱時往謁之，華甚歎異，謂曰：「君至長必為命世之器，匡難濟時者也。
sentences.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Zhang Hua had a fine eye for men; when Hui was still a child with hair in tufts he went to visit him; Hua greatly marveled and told him: “When you reach maturity you will surely be a vessel for the age, one who rights calamity and aids the times.”
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, famed for reading character, met him as a boy and said he would grow into the man who could save an era in crisis.

sentences.chinese: 」因以所服簪幘遺廆，結殷勤而別。
sentences.literal: ” Thereupon he gave Hui the hairpin-cap he himself wore, tying earnest friendship and parting.
sentences.idiomatic: He pressed his own cap on the boy as a pledge and sent him off with rare warmth.

sentences.chinese: 涉歸死，其弟耐篡位，將謀殺廆，廆亡潛以避禍。
sentences.literal: When Shegui died, his younger brother Nai usurped the seat and planned to kill Hui; Hui fled into hiding to avoid disaster.
sentences.idiomatic: After Shegui died, his brother Nai seized power and plotted murder; Hui fled into hiding.

sentences.chinese: 後國人殺耐，迎廆立之。
sentences.literal: Later the people of the state killed Nai and welcomed Hui to establish him.
sentences.idiomatic: The tribe killed Nai and brought Hui back as chief.

sentences.chinese: 初，涉歸有憾于宇文鮮卑，廆將修先君之怨，表請討之。
sentences.literal: At first Shegui had resentment toward the Yuwen Xianbei; Hui was about to settle the former lord’s grievance and memorialized requesting to campaign against them.
sentences.idiomatic: Hui wanted to avenge his father’s feud with the Yuwen and asked the court for a campaign.

sentences.chinese: 武帝弗許。
sentences.literal: Emperor Wu did not grant it.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Wu refused.

sentences.chinese: 廆怒，入寇遼西，殺略甚眾。
sentences.literal: Hui was angry; he entered and raided Liaoxi, killing and carrying off very many.
sentences.idiomatic: Enraged, he swept into Liaoxi, slaughtering and plundering widely.

sentences.chinese: 帝遣幽州諸軍討廆，戰於肥如，廆眾大敗。
sentences.literal: The Emperor dispatched the various Liaozhou armies to punish Hui; they fought at Feiru; Hui’s host was greatly defeated.
sentences.idiomatic: Imperial troops from Youzhou met him at Feiru and broke his army.

sentences.chinese: 自後復掠昌黎，每歲不絕。
sentences.literal: Thereafter he again raided Changli, every year without cease.
sentences.idiomatic: Year after year he raided Changli.

sentences.chinese: 又率眾東伐扶余，扶余王依慮自殺，廆夷其國城，驅萬餘人而歸。
sentences.literal: Again he led the host east to attack Puyŏ; King Uiryeo of Puyŏ killed himself; Hui leveled their capital walls and drove more than ten thousand people back.
sentences.idiomatic: He marched east against Puyŏ; its king killed himself; Murong sacked the capital and dragged off ten thousand captives.

sentences.chinese: 東夷校尉何龕遣督護賈沈將迎立依慮之子為王，廆遣其將孫丁率騎邀之。
sentences.literal: Colonel of the Eastern Yi He Kan sent supervisor Jia Shen with troops to welcome and establish Uiryeo’s son as king; Hui dispatched his general Sun Ding to lead cavalry and intercept them.
sentences.idiomatic: He Kan sent Jia Shen to restore the Puyŏ royal line; Murong countered with Sun Ding’s horsemen.

sentences.chinese: 沈力戰斬丁，遂復扶余之國。
sentences.literal: Shen fought hard, beheaded Ding, and thereupon restored the state of Puyŏ.
sentences.idiomatic: Jia Shen killed Sun Ding in battle and put Puyŏ back on its throne.

sentences.chinese: 廆謀於其眾曰：「吾先公以來世奉中國，且華裔理殊，強弱固別，豈能與晉競乎？
sentences.literal: Hui consulted his host saying: “From our former lords onward we have generation by generation served the Middle States; moreover Hua and Yi are different in principle, strong and weak are inherently distinct—how can we compete with Jin?
sentences.idiomatic: He told his chiefs: “Our house has long served China; steppe and heartland are not equals—we cannot stand against Jin forever.”

sentences.chinese: 何為不和以害吾百姓邪！
sentences.literal: Why can we not be at peace—must we harm our hundred surnames?
sentences.idiomatic: Why keep war and ruin our own people?”

sentences.chinese: 」乃遣使來降。
sentences.literal: ” Thereupon he dispatched envoys to come and surrender.
sentences.idiomatic: He sent envoys to offer submission.

sentences.chinese: 帝嘉之，拜為鮮卑都督。
sentences.literal: The Emperor praised him and appointed him Xianbei Area Commander.
sentences.idiomatic: The court commended him and named him commander over the Xianbei.

sentences.chinese: 廆致敬於東夷府，巾衣詣門，抗士大夫之禮。
sentences.literal: Hui paid respects at the Eastern Yi headquarters, in cap-robe went to the gate, and matched the rites of gentlemen.
sentences.idiomatic: He called at He Kan’s yamen in civil dress, observing Chinese courtesy.

sentences.chinese: 何龕嚴兵引見，廆乃改服戎衣而入。
sentences.literal: He Kan arrayed troops to lead him in; Hui thereupon changed into martial garb and entered.
sentences.idiomatic: He Kan received him under arms; Murong switched to military dress before entering.

sentences.chinese: 人問其故，廆曰：「主人不以禮，賓復何為哉！
sentences.literal: People asked the reason; Hui said: “When the host does not use ritual, what is the guest to do?
sentences.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, “If the host offers no courtesy, neither will the guest.”

sentences.chinese: 」龕聞而慚之，彌加敬憚。
sentences.literal: ” Kan heard and was ashamed, and increased reverence and awe.
sentences.idiomatic: He Kan was abashed and treated him with greater respect.

sentences.chinese: 時東胡宇文鮮卑段部以廆威德日廣，懼有吞併之計，因為寇掠，往來不絕。
sentences.literal: At that time the Eastern Hu Yuwen Xianbei and Duan division, because Hui’s might and virtue daily broadened, feared there was a plan to swallow and annex them; therefore they raided, coming and going without cease.
sentences.idiomatic: The Yuwen and Duan, fearing Murong’s growing power, raided him without pause.

sentences.chinese: 廆卑辭厚幣以撫之。
sentences.literal: Hui used humble words and thick gifts to soothe them.
sentences.idiomatic: He soothed them with humble letters and rich gifts.

sentences.chinese: 太康十年，廆又遷於徒河之青山。
sentences.literal: In the tenth year of Taikang, Hui again moved to the green hills of Tuhe.
sentences.idiomatic: In Taikang 10, Murong Hui relocated his seat to the Qing Mountains by Tuhe.

sentences.chinese: 廆以大棘城即帝顓頊之墟也，元康四年乃移居之。
sentences.literal: Hui held that great Jicheng was the ruined site of Emperor Zhuanxu; in the fourth year of Yuankang he then moved to dwell there.
sentences.idiomatic: Treating Great Jicheng as the ancient ground of Zhuanxu, he transferred his capital there in Yuankang 4.

sentences.chinese: 教以農桑，法制同于上國。
sentences.literal: He instructed them in farming and sericulture; laws and institutions matched those of the superior state.
sentences.idiomatic: He promoted tillage and mulberry culture and patterned his statutes on the Jin heartland.

sentences.chinese: 永甯中，燕垂大水，廆開倉振給，幽方獲濟。
sentences.literal: During Yongning, Yan was afflicted by great flood; Hui opened granaries to relieve and supply; the You region obtained succor.
sentences.idiomatic: When Yongning brought devastating floods to the Yan lands, Murong opened his granaries and kept the northeast from starving.

sentences.chinese: 天子聞而嘉之，褒賜命服。
sentences.literal: The Son of Heaven heard and praised him, with commendatory gifts and court dress of appointment.
sentences.idiomatic: The emperor lauded him with honors and presented insignia robes.

sentences.chinese: 太安初，宇文莫圭遣弟屈雲寇邊城，雲別帥大素延攻掠諸部，廆親擊敗之。
sentences.literal: Early in Taian, Yuwen Mogui sent his younger brother Quyun to raid a border city; Quyun’s subordinate commander Da Suyan attacked and plundered the various divisions; Hui personally struck and defeated them.
sentences.idiomatic: Early in Taian, Yuwen Mogui’s brother Quyun raided the frontier; Hui personally crushed Da Suyan’s marauding columns.

sentences.chinese: 素延怒，率眾十萬圍棘城，眾咸懼，人無距志。
sentences.literal: Suyan was angry; he led a host of one hundred thousand to surround Jicheng; the host all feared; men had no will to resist.
sentences.idiomatic: Suyan threw a hundred thousand men around Jicheng; the garrison panicked and lost the will to fight.

sentences.chinese: 廆曰：「素延雖犬羊蟻聚，然軍無法制，已在吾計中矣。
sentences.literal: Hui said: “Though Suyan is dogs-and-sheep ants-gathered, yet his army lacks law and regulation; already he is within my calculations.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong said, “Suyan’s host is a rabble without discipline—he is already playing my game.

sentences.chinese: 諸君但為力戰，無所憂也。
sentences.literal: Gentlemen, only exert yourselves in hard fighting; there is nothing to worry about.”
sentences.idiomatic: Stand fast and hit hard; leave the rest to me.”

sentences.chinese: 」乃躬貫甲胄，馳出擊之，素延大敗，追奔百里，俘斬萬餘人。
sentences.literal: ” Thereupon he personally donned armor and helmet, galloped out and struck them; Suyan was greatly defeated; pursuing the routed for one hundred li, he captured and beheaded more than ten thousand.
sentences.idiomatic: He armored himself, rode out, broke Suyan, and chased the rout a hundred li, killing or capturing over ten thousand.

sentences.chinese: 永嘉初，廆自稱鮮卑大單于。
sentences.literal: Early in Yongjia, Hui styled himself grand Shanyu of the Xianbei.
sentences.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongjia he proclaimed himself Great Shanyu of the Xianbei.

sentences.chinese: 遼東太守龐本以私憾殺東夷校尉李臻，附塞鮮卑素連、木津等托為臻報仇，實欲因而為亂，遂攻陷諸縣，殺掠士庶。
sentences.literal: Liaodong Administrator Pang Ben, out of private grievance, killed Colonel of the Eastern Yi Li Zhen; Sulian, Mujin, and others among the Xianbei attached to the frontier, on pretext of avenging Zhen, in truth wished thereby to raise rebellion; thereupon they captured and reduced various counties, killing and plundering gentlemen and commoners.
sentences.idiomatic: Pang Ben murdered Colonel Li Zhen in a private feud; frontier bands Sulian and Mujin claimed vengeance for Li but used it to rebel, storming counties and slaughtering townspeople.

sentences.chinese: 太守袁謙頻戰失利，校尉封釋懼而請和。
sentences.literal: Administrator Yuan Qian repeatedly fought with losses; Colonel Feng Shi feared and requested peace.
sentences.idiomatic: Yuan Qian kept losing battles, and Feng Shi, frightened, sued for peace.

sentences.chinese: 連歲寇掠，百姓失業，流亡歸附者日月相繼。
sentences.literal: Year after year they raided and plundered; the hundred surnames lost livelihood; refugees coming to attach followed day and night without cease.
sentences.idiomatic: Raiding went on for years, livelihoods collapsed, and displaced families arrived daily to Murong’s protection.

sentences.chinese: 廆子翰言於廆曰：「求諸侯莫如勤王，自古有為之君靡不杖此以成事業者也。
sentences.literal: Hui’s son Han spoke to Hui, saying: “To seek vassal lords is not as good as aiding the king; from antiquity, accomplished rulers have never failed to rely on this to complete enterprise.
sentences.idiomatic: His son Han urged: “Nothing secures standing like marching to rescue the throne—every founder who mattered leaned on that cause.

sentences.chinese: 今連、津跋扈，王師覆敗，蒼生屠膾，豈甚此乎！
sentences.literal: Now Sulian and Mujin are overbearing; royal armies are overturned and defeated; the black-haired folk are butchered like mince—is there aught worse than this!
sentences.idiomatic: With those two running wild, imperial forces routed, and commoners carved like meat, can ruin cut deeper?

sentences.chinese: 豎子外以龐本為名，內實幸而為寇。
sentences.literal: Those wretches outwardly use Pang Ben as their banner; inwardly they truly rejoice in being bandits.
sentences.idiomatic: They wave Pang Ben’s name abroad yet relish brigandage at heart.

sentences.chinese: 封使君以誅本請和，而毒害滋深。
sentences.literal: Commissioner Feng sought peace by executing Ben, yet poison and harm grew deeper.
sentences.idiomatic: Feng Shi’s bargain—punishing Pang Ben for peace—only deepened the harm.

sentences.chinese: 遼東傾沒，垂已二周，中原兵亂，州師屢敗，勤王杖義，今其時也。
sentences.literal: Liaodong has capsized and sunk; already two years have run their course; the Central Plain is in military chaos; provincial armies are repeatedly defeated; to aid the king and uphold righteousness—now is the hour.
sentences.idiomatic: Liaodong has been lost for two years, the heartland is torn by war, provincial hosts keep losing—now is the moment to answer the emperor’s call and seize the moral high ground.

sentences.chinese: 單于宜明九伐之威，救倒懸之命，數連、津之罪，合義兵以誅之。
sentences.literal: The Shanyu ought to manifest the majesty of the nine punishments, save lives hung inverted, enumerate the crimes of Sulian and Mujin, and join righteous troops to execute them.
sentences.idiomatic: You should wield the great powers of chastisement, rescue people from mortal peril, publish Sulian and Mujin’s crimes, and rally loyal arms to destroy them.

sentences.chinese: 上則興復遼邦，下則併吞二部，忠義彰於本朝，私利歸於我國，此則吾鴻漸之始也，終可以得志于諸侯。
sentences.literal: Above, then restore Liaodong; below, then swallow and annex the two divisions; loyalty and righteousness displayed toward this court; private profit returning to our state—this then is the beginning of our grand gradual ascent; in the end we can realize ambition among the vassal lords.
sentences.idiomatic: You recover Liaodong above, absorb the two bands below, win gratitude from Jin and strength for us—this is the first beat of the goose’s flight toward leadership among the northern lords.”

sentences.chinese: 」廆從之。
sentences.literal: ” Hui followed it.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong agreed.

sentences.chinese: 是日，率騎討連、津，大敗斬之，二部悉降，徙之棘城，立遼東郡而歸。
sentences.literal: That day he led cavalry to punish Sulian and Mujin, greatly defeated them and beheaded them; the two divisions all surrendered; he moved them to Jicheng, established Liaodong commandery, and returned.
sentences.idiomatic: That day he rode against Sulian and Mujin, slew both chiefs, resettled their people at Jicheng, founded Liaodong commandery, and came home.

sentences.chinese: 懷帝蒙塵于平陽，王浚承制以廆為散騎常侍、冠軍將軍、前鋒大都督、大單于，廆不受。
sentences.literal: Emperor Huai suffered dust at Pingyang; Wang Jun, acting on commission, made Hui Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, General Who Guards the Crown, Grand Area Commander of the Vanguard, and Grand Shanyu; Hui did not accept.
sentences.idiomatic: While Emperor Huai languished in Pingyang, Wang Jun offered Murong a cluster of honors culminating in Great Shanyu; Murong declined them all.

sentences.chinese: 建興中，湣帝遣使拜廆鎮軍將軍、昌黎、遼東二國公。
sentences.literal: During Jianxing, Emperor Min dispatched envoys to appoint Hui General Who Garrisons the Army and duke of the two states of Changli and Liaodong.
sentences.idiomatic: Under Jianxing, Emperor Min named him General Who Garrisons the Army and duke over both Changli and Liaodong.

sentences.chinese: 建武初，元帝承制拜廆假節、散騎常侍、都督遼左雜夷流人諸軍事、龍驤將軍、大單于、昌黎公，廆讓而不受。
sentences.literal: Early in Jianwu, Emperor Yuan, acting on commission, appointed Hui acting credentials, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, Area Commander of military affairs of the miscellaneous Yi and displaced persons to the left of Liaodong, General of Dragon Soaring, Grand Shanyu, and Duke of Changli; Hui declined and did not accept.
sentences.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu, Emperor Yuan vested him with plenary frontier command, the Dragon-Soaring generalship, the Grand Shanyu title, and the Changli dukedom; Murong again demurred.

sentences.chinese: 征虜將軍魯昌說廆曰：「今兩京傾沒，天子蒙塵，琅邪承制江東，實人命所系。
sentences.literal: General Who Subdues Invaders Lu Chang urged Hui, saying: “Now the two capitals have capsized and sunk; the Son of Heaven suffers dust; Langya receives commission east of the Long River; truly the thread of men’s lives hangs thereon.
sentences.idiomatic: Lu Chang argued: “Luoyang and Chang’an are gone and the sovereign is a captive; Prince Langya’s court on the lower Yangtze is where fate now turns.

sentences.chinese: 明公雄據海朔，跨總一方，而諸部猶怙眾稱兵，未遵道化者，蓋以官非王命，又自以為強。
sentences.literal: Illustrious lord heroically holds the sea north, straddling and overseeing one quarter; yet the various divisions still rely on numbers and raise arms, not complying with civilizing guidance—this is because offices lack kingly mandate, and moreover they deem themselves strong.
sentences.idiomatic: You dominate the northern coast, yet tribes still defy you because your posts lack formal Jin sanction and they trust their own strength.

sentences.chinese: 今宜通使琅邪，勸承大統，然後敷宣帝命，以伐有罪，誰敢不從！
sentences.literal: Now it is fitting to open envoys to Langya, urge assumption of the great succession; thereafter spread abroad the emperor’s command to punish the guilty—who dares not follow!”
sentences.idiomatic: Send envoys to Langya, urge him to take the throne, then march with genuine imperial writ—who would refuse!”

sentences.chinese: 」廆善之，乃遣其長史王濟浮海勸進。
sentences.literal: ” Hui thought it good; thereupon he dispatched his chief clerk Wang Ji by sea to urge advancement.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong approved and sent Chief Clerk Wang Ji across the sea to urge Sima Rui to ascend.

sentences.chinese: 及帝即尊位，遣謁者陶遼重申前命，授廆將軍、單于，廆固辭公封。
sentences.literal: When the Emperor assumed the honored seat, he dispatched Herald Tao Liao to reaffirm the prior commands, investing Hui as general and Shanyu; Hui firmly declined ducal enfeoffment.
sentences.idiomatic: After Sima Rui took the throne, Herald Tao Liao renewed the grant of general and Shanyu; Murong still refused the ducal patent.

sentences.chinese: 時二京傾覆，幽、冀淪陷，廆刑政修明，虛懷引納，流亡士庶多繈負歸之。
sentences.literal: At that time the two capitals overturned, You and Ji sank and fell; Hui’s punishments and government were cultivated and clear; with open bosom he drew in and accepted; many displaced gentlemen and commoners, babies swaddled on backs, returned to him.
sentences.idiomatic: With both capitals lost and Hebei overrun, Murong’s clean government and open door drew exiles—infants bundled on backs and all.

sentences.chinese: 廆乃立郡以統流人，冀州人為冀陽郡，豫州人為成周郡，青州人為營丘郡，并州人為唐國郡。
sentences.literal: Hui thereupon established commanderies to oversee displaced persons: people of Jizhou as Jiyang commandery; people of Yuzhou as Chengzhou commandery; people of Qingzhou as Yingqiu commandery; people of Bingzhou as Tangguo commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: He organized refugees by homeland—Jiyang for Jizhou people, Chengzhou for Yuzhou, Yingqiu for Qingzhou, Tangguo for Bingzhou.

sentences.chinese: 於是推舉賢才，委以庶政，以河東裴嶷、代郡魯昌、北平陽耽為謀主，北海逢羨、廣平遊邃、北平西方虔、渤海封抽、西河宋奭、河東裴開為股肱，渤海封弈、平原宋該、安定皇甫岌、蘭陵繆愷以文章才俊任居樞要，會稽硃左車、太山胡毋翼、魯國孔纂以舊德清重引為賓友，平原劉贊儒學該通，引為東庠祭酒，其世子皝率國胄束修受業焉。
sentences.literal: Thereupon he promoted worthy talents, entrusting them with myriad government; he made Pei Yi of Hedong, Lu Chang of Dai commandery, and Yang Dan of Beiping chief strategists; Feng Xian of Beihai, You Sui of Guangping, Xifang Qian of Beiping, Feng Chou of Bohai, Song Shi of Xihe, and Pei Kai of Hedong arm-and-thigh ministers; Feng Yi of Bohai, Song Gai of Pingyuan, Huangfu Ji of Anding, and Miao Kai of Lanling, by literary talent, held posts at the pivot; Zhu Zuoche of Kuaiji, Hu Wuyi of Taishan, and Kong Zuan of Lu, by old virtue pure and weighty, were brought in as guest-friends; Liu Zan of Pingyuan, Confucian learning comprehensive, was appointed libationer of the eastern school; his heir apparent Huang led scions of the state with bundled tuition to receive instruction therein.
sentences.idiomatic: He elevated talent across the board: Pei Yi, Lu Chang, and Yang Dan directed strategy; Feng Xian, You Sui, Xifang Qian, Feng Chou, Song Shi, and Pei Kai ran the administration; Feng Yi, Song Gai, Huangfu Ji, and Miao Kai held key literary posts; Zhu Zuoche, Hu Wuyi, and Kong Zuan were honored as mentors; Liu Zan, a thorough Confucian scholar, became dean of the eastern academy, where heir Murong Huang and young nobles studied.

sentences.chinese: 廆覽政之暇，親臨聽之，於是路有頌聲，禮讓興矣。
sentences.literal: In the leisure of Hui’s reviewing government, he personally came and listened; thereupon on the roads there were songs of praise, and ritual yielding arose.
sentences.idiomatic: When duties allowed, he attended the lectures himself, and the domain gained a name for courtesy and deference.

sentences.chinese: 時平州刺史、東夷校尉崔毖自以為南州士望，意存懷集，而流亡者莫有赴之。
sentences.literal: At that time Cui Bi, Inspector of Pingzhou and Colonel of the Eastern Yi, deemed himself the gentry expectation of the southern provinces, intending to cherish and gather, yet among displaced persons none came to him.
sentences.idiomatic: Cui Bi, confident in his southern pedigree, meant to rally refugees, yet none joined him.

sentences.chinese: 毖意廆拘留，乃陰結高句麗及宇文、段國等，謀滅廆以分其地。
sentences.literal: Bi suspected Hui was detaining them; thereupon he secretly allied Goguryeo with Yuwen, the Duan state, and others, plotting to destroy Hui and divide his land.
sentences.idiomatic: He blamed Murong for poaching his following and secretly enlisted Goguryeo, the Yuwen, and the Duan to carve up Murong’s territory.

sentences.chinese: 太興初，三國伐廆，廆曰：「彼信崔毖虛說，邀一時之利，烏合而來耳。
sentences.literal: Early in Taixing, the three states campaigned against Hui; Hui said: “They trust Cui Bi’s empty talk and seek momentary profit; they are a crow-flock come together.
sentences.idiomatic: When the triple alliance struck in Taixing, Murong said, “They chase Cui Bi’s lies and a quick gain—nothing but a mob.

sentences.chinese: 既無統一，莫相歸伏，吾今破之必矣。
sentences.literal: Since there is no unified command, none submit to one another; I now break them—surely.
sentences.idiomatic: With no single hand on the reins, they will not trust one another—I can crush them.

sentences.chinese: 然彼軍初合，其鋒甚銳，幸我速戰。
sentences.literal: Yet their army first united, its edge very keen; they hope I fight speedily.
sentences.idiomatic: Their first rush is fierce—they want me to meet them at once.

sentences.chinese: 若逆擊之，落其計矣。
sentences.literal: If I strike them head-on, I fall into their plan.
sentences.idiomatic: A hasty counterblow would walk straight into their trap.

sentences.chinese: 靖以待之，必懷疑貳，迭相猜防。
sentences.literal: Be still and await them; surely they will harbor suspicion and duplicity, repeatedly suspecting and guarding one another.
sentences.idiomatic: Hold still and they will grow wary, eyeing each other.

sentences.chinese: 一則疑吾與毖譎而覆之，二則自疑三國之中與吾有韓魏之謀者，待其人情沮惑，然後取之必矣。
sentences.literal: On the one hand they will suspect I am treacherous with Bi and will overturn them; on the other they will suspect that among the three states one holds Han-and-Wei-style plotting with me; when their men’s hearts are dejected and confused, then taking them—surely.”
sentences.idiomatic: They will wonder whether I collude with Cui Bi or which partner is secretly dealing with me like Han and Wei against the rest; once doubt gnaws them hollow, we win.”

sentences.chinese: 」於是三國攻棘城，廆閉門不戰，遣使送牛酒以犒宇文，大言於眾曰：「崔毖昨有使至。
sentences.literal: ” Thereupon the three states attacked Jicheng; Hui closed the gates and did not fight; he dispatched envoys presenting cattle and ale to feast the Yuwen, loudly saying to the host: “Cui Bi yesterday had an envoy arrive.”
sentences.idiomatic: The allies surrounded Jicheng; Murong barred the gates and sent beef and wine to the Yuwen camp, proclaiming, “Cui Bi’s messenger came only yesterday.”

sentences.chinese: 」於是二國果疑宇文同於廆也，引兵而歸。
sentences.literal: Thereupon the two states indeed suspected the Yuwen was of one mind with Hui; they led troops and withdrew.
sentences.idiomatic: Goguryeo and the Duan decided the Yuwen had sided with Murong and marched off.

sentences.chinese: 宇文悉獨官曰：「二國雖歸，吾當獨兼其國，何用人為！
sentences.literal: Yuwen Xiduguan said: “Though the two states return, I ought alone to annex his state—what need of others!
sentences.idiomatic: Xiduguan growled, “Let them go—I will take Murong’s realm by myself.

sentences.chinese: 」盡眾逼城，連營三十里。
sentences.literal: ” He employed the entire host pressing the city; connected camps thirty li.
sentences.idiomatic: He threw every man against the walls, camps stretching thirty li.

sentences.chinese: 廆簡銳士配皝，推鋒於前；
sentences.literal: Hui selected crack warriors, assigning them to Huang, pushing spear-points in front;
sentences.idiomatic: Murong gave picked troops to Murong Huang to spearhead the attack;

sentences.chinese: 翰領精騎為奇兵，從旁出，直沖其營；
sentences.literal: Han led picked cavalry as odd troops, emerging from the side, straight charging their camp;
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Han swept in with elite horse as a flanking column straight at the Yuwen camp;

sentences.chinese: 廆方陣而進。
sentences.literal: Hui advanced in square formations.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong himself advanced in ordered squares.

sentences.chinese: 悉獨官自恃其眾，不設備，見廆軍之至，方率兵距之。
sentences.literal: Xiduguan relied on his numbers, set no preparations; seeing Hui’s army arrive, only then led troops to resist.
sentences.idiomatic: Trusting his host, Xiduguan posted no pickets and only scrambled to meet Murong when the lines closed.

sentences.chinese: 前鋒始交，翰已入其營，縱火焚之，其眾皆震擾，不知所為，遂大敗，悉獨官僅以身免，盡俘其眾。
sentences.literal: The vanguard had but begun clashing when Han already entered their camp, set fire and burned it; their host all trembled and stirred, not knowing what to do; thereupon they were greatly defeated; Xiduguan barely escaped with his body; all his host was captured.
sentences.idiomatic: The first clash barely started when Han torched the camp; the Yuwen melted in panic, Xiduguan fled alone, and his army was taken whole.

sentences.chinese: 於是營候獲皇帝玉璽三紐，遣長史裴嶷送於建鄴。
sentences.literal: Thereupon camp sentries obtained three cords of the emperor’s jade seal; he dispatched chief clerk Pei Yi to deliver them to Jianye.
sentences.idiomatic: Patrols recovered three imperial jade seals; Chief Clerk Pei Yi carried them to Jiankang.

sentences.chinese: 崔毖懼廆之仇己也，使兄子燾偽賀廆。
sentences.literal: Cui Bi feared Hui’s enmity toward himself; he had his elder brother’s son Tao falsely congratulate Hui.
sentences.idiomatic: Fearing Murong’s vengeance, Cui Bi sent his nephew Cui Tao with hollow congratulations.

sentences.chinese: 會三國使亦至請和，曰：「非我本意也，崔平州教我耳。
sentences.literal: It happened the three states’ envoys also arrived requesting peace, saying: “It was not our original intent; Inspector Cui of Pingzhou taught us.”
sentences.idiomatic: The allied envoys came suing for peace, pleading, “We never meant it—Inspector Cui told us to.”

sentences.chinese: 」廆將燾示以攻圍之處，臨之以兵，曰：「汝叔父教三國滅我，何以詐來賀我乎？
sentences.literal: Hui led Tao and showed him the places of attack and siege, pressing him with troops, saying: “Your uncle taught the three states to destroy me—how do you falsely come congratulate me?”
sentences.idiomatic: Murong marched Tao to the siege lines under arms: “Your uncle set three powers on me—why this sham goodwill?”

sentences.chinese: 」廆懼，首服。
sentences.literal: Tao trembled and acknowledged his deceit.
sentences.idiomatic: Tao was terrified and confessed.

sentences.chinese: 廆乃遣燾歸說毖曰：「降者上策，走者下策也。
sentences.literal: Hui thereupon sent Tao back to persuade Bi, saying: “To surrender is the upper strategy; to flee is the lower strategy.”
sentences.idiomatic: Murong sent Tao back with an ultimatum: surrender was the high road, flight the ruinous course.

sentences.chinese: 」以兵隨之。
sentences.literal: He sent troops following him.
sentences.idiomatic: Troops trailed the mission.

sentences.chinese: 毖與數十騎棄家室奔於高句麗，廆悉降其眾，徙燾及高瞻等於棘城，待以賓禮。
sentences.literal: Bi with several dozen cavalry abandoned household and fled to Goguryeo; Hui entirely subdued his host, moved Tao and Gao Zhan and others to Jicheng, treating them with guest rites.
sentences.idiomatic: Cui Bi bolted to Goguryeo with a few dozen riders; Murong absorbed his followers and resettled Tao and Gao Zhan at Jicheng with guest courtesy.

sentences.chinese: 明年，高句麗寇遼東，廆遣眾擊敗之。
sentences.literal: The next year Goguryeo raided Liaodong; Hui dispatched a host and defeated them.
sentences.idiomatic: The following year he turned back a Goguryeo raid on Liaodong.

sentences.chinese: 裴嶷至自建鄴，帝遣使者拜廆監平州諸軍事、安北將軍、平州刺史，增邑二千戶。
sentences.literal: Pei Yi arrived from Jianye; the Emperor dispatched envoys to appoint Hui to supervise military affairs of Pingzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Pingzhou, increasing fief by two thousand households.
sentences.idiomatic: When Pei Yi returned from the capital, the court named Murong governor-general of Pingzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, and added two thousand households to his fief.

sentences.chinese: 尋加使持節、都督幽州東夷諸軍事、車騎將軍、平州牧，進封遼東郡公，邑一萬戶，常侍、單于並如故；
sentences.literal: Shortly he was further appointed credential-bearing envoy, Area Commander of military affairs of Youzhou and the Eastern Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Shepherd of Pingzhou, promoted to Duke of Liaodong commandery with a fief of ten thousand households, while his posts as Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary and Shanyu remained unchanged.
sentences.idiomatic: Soon he also received the staff of authority, command over Youzhou and the eastern tribes, the chariot-and-cavalry generalship, the governorship of Pingzhou, and elevation to Duke of Liaodong at ten thousand households, keeping his palace appointment and Shanyu title.

sentences.chinese: 丹書鐵券，承制海東，命備官司，置平州守宰。
sentences.literal: He was granted the cinnabar writ and iron tally, commissioned with discretionary authority east of the sea, ordered to complete the official apparatus, and empowered to appoint Pingzhou magistrates.
sentences.idiomatic: He was also given the vermilion warrant and iron covenant, delegated full discretion on the Liaodong shore, and charged with staffing Pingzhou government.

sentences.chinese: 段末波初統其國，而不修備，廆遣皝襲之，入令支，收其名馬寶物而還。
sentences.literal: Duan Mobo first ruled his state yet did not cultivate preparations; Hui dispatched Huang to raid them, entered Lingzhi, collected their famous horses and precious goods, and returned.
sentences.idiomatic: Duan Mobo, newly in power, left his borders slack; Murong Huang struck Lingzhi and came away with prized horses and treasure.

sentences.chinese: 石勒遣使通和，廆距之。
sentences.literal: Shi Le dispatched envoys to open peace; Hui refused them.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Le sent envoys seeking friendship; Murong turned them away.

sentences.chinese: 送其使於建鄴。
sentences.literal: He sent their envoys to Jianye.
sentences.idiomatic: He forwarded Shi Le’s envoys to Jiankang.
